title: Cocoa butter: what it is and what kinds of fat it contains

seo.title: Cocoa butter: what it is and what fats it contains
seo.meta_description: Cocoa butter is the natural fat in cocoa beans. See its saturated, monounsaturated, and polyunsaturated fat profile and the fatty acids that dominate.
seo.search_intent: Understand what cocoa butter is and its fatty-acid composition

excerpt: Cocoa butter is essentially 100% fat. The USDA reference contains about 59.7% saturated fat, 32.9% monounsaturated fat, and 3% polyunsaturated fat. Stearic, oleic, and palmitic acids make up most of it.
content_html:
Cocoa butter is not a chocolate-flavored spread. It is the natural fat inside the cocoa bean. When cocoa mass is pressed to make cocoa powder, some of that fat is separated as cocoa butter.

It is also central to chocolate's texture: firm at room temperature, yet able to melt rapidly near body temperature.

What cocoa butter contains

The USDA reference for cocoa butter contains 100 g fat and about 884 calories per 100 g, with essentially no protein, carbohydrate, or fiber. Nutritionally it behaves like a pure fat, but its fatty-acid pattern is distinctive.

Saturated, monounsaturated, and polyunsaturated fat

Fat typePer 100 g
Saturated59.7 g
Monounsaturated32.9 g
Polyunsaturated3.0 g

The rows do not total exactly 100 g because total fat includes additional lipid fractions and minor components beyond those broad fatty-acid sums.

Three fatty acids dominate

The largest individual fats are stearic acid at about 33.2 g/100 g, oleic acid at about 32.6 g, and palmitic acid at about 25.4 g.

Together those three account for more than 90% of cocoa butter's weight in the reference. Exact proportions shift somewhat with cocoa variety, climate, and growing region.

Why it is solid despite so much oleic acid

Chocolate texture depends not only on which fatty acids are present but also on how they are arranged into triglycerides and crystals. Cocoa butter can crystallize in several forms.

Tempering encourages a stable form that gives finished chocolate gloss, a clean snap, and controlled melting. Heat cycling or poor storage can reorganize those crystals and contribute to fat bloom.

What a practical amount looks like

Ten grams of cocoa butter provides about 88 calories and 6 g saturated fat. In a chocolate bar, the final amount depends on how much cocoa butter is combined with cocoa mass, cocoa powder, sugar, and any other ingredients.

That is why cacao percentage alone cannot tell you saturated fat. Two 70% bars can distribute their cocoa-derived ingredients differently.

Bottom line

Cocoa butter is the bean's own fat, dominated by stearic, oleic, and palmitic acids. Chemically it is mostly saturated fat, with roughly one-third monounsaturated fat. The same profile that matters nutritionally also explains much of chocolate's unusual melting and crystallization behavior.

faq.question: Does cocoa butter contain sugar?
faq.answer: Essentially no. Cocoa butter is the fat fraction of the cocoa bean; sugar in chocolate is added separately.

faq.question: Is cocoa butter mostly saturated fat?
faq.answer: Yes. The USDA reference is about 59.7% saturated fat, followed by 32.9% monounsaturated fat.

faq.question: Which fatty acid is most abundant?
faq.answer: Stearic acid is about 33.2 g/100 g and oleic acid about 32.6 g/100 g, so the two are very close.

faq.question: Is cocoa butter the same as cocoa powder?
faq.answer: No. Cocoa butter is the fat fraction. Cocoa powder is made from the solids left after part of that fat is pressed out.
